correctness.rationale: The full space has polyanalytic expansion ∑_{j<n} z̄^j f_j(z) with holomorphic f_j (iterate the distributional Cauchy–Riemann equation). At nonnegative rotation frequency ξ this gives exactly r^ξe^{iξθ} times a polynomial in r² of degree <n; negative frequencies give only a finite-dimensional exceptional sum. Radial compression preserves those spaces. With x=ξ(1−r²) and ρ=α+j+k+1, the rescaled unsigned Gram entry is ξ^ρ Beta(ξ+1,ρ)→Γ(ρ); replacing the symbol by the pure power gives the same expression with ρ+σ and the factor b. The remainder after subtracting that power is bounded by ε(1−r²)^σ almost everywhere near the boundary, giving at most ε times a uniformly bounded rescaled moment, with exponentially small interior tail even after polynomial scaling. This justifies the matrix limit also for essential boundary limits and complex b. Passing to an orthonormal frame gives the norm limit bB^(−1/2)AB^(−1/2); its singular values are |b|μ_i. The decaying block norms imply compactness, and counting integers for each of the finitely many positive branches gives the stated counting asymptotic; inversion, the p-series test and harmonic summation give all three endpoint statements. At σ=1 the multiplication compression is the Laguerre Jacobi matrix; its trace is n(n+α). For n=2, α=0 the determinant of A−μB is μ²−4μ+2 at σ=1 and μ²−16μ+12 at σ=2. Thus the coefficient for the quadratic symbol is 16+2√12, whereas squaring the positive first-order operator gives 4²=16. These checks replay RESULT.md lines 30–74. CHECK.py was read, not run; its finite beta-moment comparisons are corroboration only.
